newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent bounces higher with transatlantic pull.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent bounces higher with transatlantic pull.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude values recovered earlier losses in late afternoon trade on Friday, helped by an open arbitrage to the U.S., while differentials for other grades held steady.
The sole Brent cargo to turn wet today was kept by a trading house and resold to a Wall Street trader at Jan Brent +49 cents, some five cents above Tuesday's highest traded level.
The buyer is thought to be holding at least three Brents already and is believed to be working a VLCC transatlantic.
Another Brent, loading Dec 17-19 traded earlier between two majors at Jan Brent +35 cents.
Jan Brent values recovered some earlier losses inspired by bearish U.S. stock data and IPE futures were trading close to Tuesday's settlement, around $23.75/$23.60 a barrel, by 1730 GMT.
Intermonth spreads came off earlier highs but were talked talked firmer than Tuesday's levels. Jan/Feb was discussed either side of +70 cents, with Feb/March at +61/64 cents.
CFDs were slow to react to the higher Brent deal, with this week's dates bid at Jan Brent +29 and next week at Jan Brent +23/+32, having traded at +25 cents earlier.
